claims.text: An HEA containing a minimal fraction of Pt together with Ni, Co, and Mo will have greater HER activity than conventional Pt-based catalysts.
The proposed HEA will have greater HOR activity than conventional Pt-based catalysts.
The proposed HEA will have greater HER durability than conventional Pt-based catalysts.
The proposed HEA will have greater HOR durability than conventional Pt-based catalysts.
The initial material is a disordered multi-principal-element alloy lacking specifically optimized hydrogen-catalytic sites.
Alloying a small amount of Pt with Ni, Co, and Mo will modulate the alloy's electronic structure.
Alloying a small amount of Pt with Ni, Co, and Mo will modulate lattice strain.
Synergistic interactions arising from the HEA's complex elemental makeup will stabilize catalytically active sites.
Controlled lattice strain and modified electronic properties will contribute to stabilization of active sites.
Introducing a low fraction of Pt into the transition-metal matrix will shift the d-band center.
The Pt-induced electronic change will optimize hydrogen-binding energies.
Transition metals adjacent to Pt will enhance corrosion resistance.
Transition metals adjacent to Pt will prevent active-site degradation during long-term electrochemical cycling.
The modified HEA will exhibit lower overpotentials than traditional Pt catalysts.
The modified HEA will exhibit improved Tafel slopes and higher exchange-current densities than traditional Pt catalysts.
The modified HEA will retain catalytic performance better during prolonged operation than traditional Pt catalysts.
Conventional Pt-based catalysts have high intrinsic HER and HOR activity.
Conventional Pt-based catalysts have compromised durability during extended operation.
The magnitude of performance improvement is sensitive to elemental ratios and synthesis parameters.

contradictions.description: The central hypothesis requires improved activity and durability for both HER and HOR, whereas the falsification rule only clearly rejects the material when statistically significant improvements are absent in both the broad activity and durability categories. Failure in one required category or in only one reaction would not necessarily trigger falsification.
